classification.difficultyReason: Open cylinder with a face omitted, diameter to radius, then number of cans; same demand as p28-q5.

content.prompt:
Mia is painting a water tank in the shape of a cylinder $2.5\text{ m}$ tall and $4\text{ m}$ in diameter.
The outside of the tank is to be painted, excluding the base.
If a two-litre can of paint covers $15\text{ m}^2$, find the number of cans needed.

answer.worked:
The base is excluded; paint the curved wall and circular top.
$$\begin{align*}
r&=4\div2=2\text{ m}\\
A&=2\pi rh+\pi r^2\\
A&=2\pi(2)(2.5)+\pi(2)^2\\
A&=14\pi\text{ m}^2\approx44.0\text{ m}^2\\
\text{Cans required}&=\frac{14\pi}{15}\approx2.9
\end{align*}$$
Round up to buy enough paint: $3$ cans.
